quest.title: They Once Walked the Starry Sky
quest.description:
"They will descend upon the 'Cliff of Prophecy'..."

Thus would the epics of later generations speak of this time:
The heroes leaped light of foot o'er floral cliffs, trials and tribulations besting forthwith. By their arm they brought forth rain and dew, the dark clouds fled, and flowers grew.

Comment in the margins: You forgot to mention how popular the forest tavern was.
Comment below the comment: Wait, did all of you think the wine was good? I thought it tasted kinda weird.
Comment below the comment below the comment: That might be because someone put... into your cup... (the following words are scratched out)
quest.rewards_formatted: Primogem x20, Mora x20000, Hero's Wit x2, Mystic Enhancement Ore x4

chapter.num: Summertide Scales and Tales: Page II
chapter.title: They Once Walked the Starry Sky

talks.objective: Wait until morning the next day (08:00 – 12:00)
Go to the Forest of Blessings Rail Station platform

dialogues.speaker: Almond
dialogues.text: Get up, Cedule! Time to get to work, you lazybones!

dialogues.speaker: Cedule
dialogues.text: Uh... Can't... can't remember how to call the train. Just lemme sleep a little longer, then I'm sure I'll remember...

dialogues.speaker: Almond
dialogues.text: Don't try to pull one over on me, young man! Your Fading Disorder has been cured! I saw you chugging cup after cup of Magic Tonic in the Tavern last night.

dialogues.speaker: Cedule
dialogues.text: Uh... You must be mistaken, Grandpa Almond. That guy definitely wasn't me...

dialogues.speaker: Almond
dialogues.text: Oh, you remember my name now, do you? Then it seems like you're all better — you had no idea who I was when you were fading. Now, enough of your nonsense, get up! The Fairy and her friends are going to be here any second!

dialogues.speaker: Cedule
dialogues.text: Alright, I'm up, I'm up... The Maritime Express should be here soon.

dialogues.speaker: Almond
dialogues.text: Hmph, that's more like it. Lie there any longer and you'll start gathering dust!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is everything okay?

dialogues.speaker: Almond
dialogues.text: #The Hero, {M#his}{F#her} pixie companion, and the Forest Fairy! I didn't know you were already here. Oh, merciful macadamias... I'm sorry you had to see that.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's alright! Paimon knows the feeling! Who doesn't want to sleep in first thing in the morning?

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Does the Maritime Express run out of Constellation Metropole?

dialogues.speaker: Almond
dialogues.text: Yes. Each train needs a conductor to operate, and the conductors are always from the capital. The more difficult maneuvers are a little too complicated when you're made of paper.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh... so you mean, the people of Constellation Metropole aren't origami animals like you?

dialogues.speaker: Almond
dialogues.text: Well, the city welcomes visitors from all over the world, so you're bound to run into some Forest-dwellers there. But yes, generally speaking, the residents of Constellation Metropole look quite different from us.

dialogues.speaker: Almond
dialogues.text: Ah, you'll see for yourself soon enough... Here comes the train.

dialogues.speaker: Wheel
dialogues.text: Pleasure to meet you, everyone. My name is Wheel, and I'll be the conductor for your journey today. I'm assuming you're the ones who called the train?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa... it's a little toy man!

dialogues.speaker: Almond
dialogues.text: Yes, we called the train. The Hero and the Forest Fairy need a ride to Constellation Metropole.

dialogues.speaker: Wheel
dialogues.text: The... The Hero and the Forest Fairy!? The ones from the prophecy?

dialogues.speaker: Wheel
dialogues.text: Wh—Why didn't you say so earlier? We could've prepared a far more luxurious train... I—I'll just go back and get a better one!

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: That's okay, Mr. Wheel. We're trying to get to the city as fast as possible. We just need you to get us across the sea. In your capable hands, I'm sure we'll get there in no time!

dialogues.speaker: Wheel
dialogues.text: O—Of course, my lady. It would be an honor!

dialogues.speaker: Wheel
dialogues.text: Well then, all aboard! Sit anywhere you like. We'll get a stunning view of Simulanka no matter where you're seated!
Hehehe... Breakfast...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm? Did one of you just say something?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Not me...

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Wasn't me, either.
Breakfast... No, come back...

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Hmm... Sounds like the voice is coming from inside the train.

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: Hehe... Fish... Chicken drumsticks... Got ya...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What the... What's Kirara doing here!?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Eating her own tail, apparently...

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: Nom nom meow...

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Is she a friend of yours?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, let Paimon introduce you... This is Kirara, she's— Wait, actually, maybe we should wake her up first.

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: Meow... So noisy... Mrrow!? Is it morning already...?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Good meowning.

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: #Hm, morning... Huh? Huuuuuuh!? {NICKNAME}! Paimon! It's... It's you!

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: Which means... Oh, thank goodness! It was all a dream after all! Ehehehe, gotta hand it to my imagination, it all felt super real! There were these toy people, but they were alive, and they could talk...

dialogues.speaker: Wheel
dialogues.text: Ahem... Madame, sleeping overnight in the train car is prohibited...

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: Mrrow!? It... It wasn't just a dream?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's alright, Kirara... Apparently, we're in a world called "Simulanka." We got here yesterday, too.

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: Simulanka? So, that's what it's called. I spent all day yesterday wandering around this one city... The toy people called it Constellation Metropole. I was trying to find a way to get back home.

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: I was seriously starting to think I'd gotten on the bad side of some great youkai, and gotten swallowed whole...

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Ah... I take it you're Inazuman, then, Miss Kirara?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: She sure is! But, uh... Kirara, here, is kinda special. Let Paimon introduce you for real this time. Kirara is a nekomata from Inazuma. She works as a courier for Komaniya Express.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Ah, nice to meet you! I'm Nilou, a member of Zubayr Theater. You can usually find us performing in Sumeru City's Grand Bazaar. Right now, though... I suppose I should introduce myself as the Fairy of the Forest of Blessings!

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: Oh, you're Nilou! I've heard a lot about you from my deliveries in Sumeru. I even saw one of your performances back in the day! You're an amazing dancer. But, uh, did you say you were a... Forest Fairy?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, that's her new identity here in Simulanka. Speaking of new identities, looks like you've got a new outfit yourself, Kirara...

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: Yeah, I know! It confused the heck out of me yesterday... I just woke up in a set of brand-new clothes I'd never seen before.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That must mean you have a big part to play here, too!

response.speaker: Kirara
response.text: I think Miss Lynette would be better suited to that role, being a magician and all...

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: Did you by any chance hear a voice speaking to you before you got here, Miss Kirara?

response.speaker: Kirara
response.text: A voice... Oh, yeah, I did hear something, but I was so freaked out, my tails got all tangled. So I... didn't catch much of what was said, hehe...

response.speaker: Chestnut
response.text: S—S—Sorry for the interruption...

response.speaker: Chestnut
response.text: B—But this nekomata friend of yours... She doesn't eat hamsters, does she?

response.speaker: Firecracker
response.text: O—Or frogs...?

response.speaker: Kirara
response.text: Oh, no need to worry, little guys! I would never do something like that! Well, unless I'd been out in the wild too long without anything to eat. Huh, speaking of eating, I am getting a little hungry...

response.speaker: Almond
response.text: Ahem! Where are your manners, everyone!? This young lady is a trusted friend of our esteemed Hero!

response.speaker: Almond
response.text: Now, I know a fear of felines is etched into us with ink, but I'm certain Miss Nekomata-in-Boots here means us no harm!

response.speaker: Cedule
response.text: Sure looks like you're keeping your distance, though, Grandpa Almond...

response.speaker: Kirara
response.text: You all have nothing to fear, I promise! I met some origami animals in Constellation Metropole yesterday, and I even made sure to retract my claws so I didn't hurt them by accident.

response.speaker: Kirara
response.text: Plus, you all look just about as tasty as the cardboard boxes I deliver, haha... Uhh, not that I'd try to eat you even if you did look tasty! Promise!

response.speaker: Almond
response.text: ...Please excuse us, Ma'am. It's just an unconscious reaction.

response.speaker: Wheel
response.text: Ahem, dear passengers... It's almost time for us to depart...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh yeah, that. Whoops, this turned into a pretty long conversation, didn't it... Alright, let's get on the train! You coming with us, Kirara?

response.speaker: Kirara
response.text: Mhm, I'll ride with you to the next stop. There's a place near the Metropole that caught my eye yesterday, so I want to go explore it today.

response.speaker: Almond
response.text: Then all that remains for me to say is: On behalf of the Forest of Blessings, thank you, once again, for all you've done for us.

response.speaker: Almond
response.text: May the Goddess of Fate be with you and bless your journey, Madame Fairy, Miss Nekomata-in-Boots, and our brave Heroes.

response.speaker: Almond
response.text: Please do visit us in the Forest of Blessings again, once peace has returned to this land!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We will! We'll definitely meet again!

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: Take care, Grandpa Almond!

response.speaker: Kirara
response.text: Is... Is that a thing? I guess I am wearing a pair of boots, but still...

talks.objective: Connect the train carriages
Go to the Forest of Blessings Rail Station platform
Talk to the conductor and prepare to depart
Ride the Maritime Express to Constellation Metropole
Reach Constellation Metropole Station

dialogues.speaker: Wheel
dialogues.text: Here we are! Constellation Metropole is right over there. It's a short walk from here to the Gear Sky Ladder, which will take you right to Metropole Square. Thank you again for choosing the Maritime Express!

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Great. And thanks to you for a smooth and pleasant journey, Mr. Wheel.

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: The train cars were comfortable and spacious, and I had a great night's sleep. I'll definitely be back!

dialogues.speaker: Wheel
dialogues.text: Um... As you wish, Ma'am.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Where should we go next? Is that place you wanted to check out nearby?

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: Mhm, I took a walk around yesterday and it felt like there was something weird about it. So I think I'll indulge my curiosity and go investigate.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Want us to come with you?

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: It's okay — you guys go ahead and visit the Metropole for now. Hopefully that's where you'll be able to find out some more about this world.

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: I pretty much explored the whole place from the rooftops yesterday, but for some reason, this is the place that caught my attention.

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: Hehe, you know what I mean, right? Like, when you get a stone stuck in your claw, or something. It keeps nagging you to dig it out, and you can't focus on anything else until you do.

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: But don't worry — if you run into any trouble, I'll be there faster than you can say "Gold-Level Courier of the Komaniya Express"!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay, fair enough. We'll head to the Metropole then. Guess this is where we say bye for now.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Stay safe, Kirara.

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: Mhm! Don't worry about me — let's not forget I'm a youkai!

talks.objective: Go to the Gear Sky Ladder

dialogues.speaker: Bleufond
dialogues.text: Help me! Help... Oh Goddess of Prophecy above, could you kind souls please help us?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What happened here? Why are you all suspended in midair...?

dialogues.speaker: Bleufond
dialogues.text: I mean, being stuck in midair still beats falling to the ground and being smashed into a pile of blocks... Ugh, I told him to be careful, but— No, never mind, now's not the time for that.

dialogues.speaker: Bleufond
dialogues.text: My good friends, could I trouble you to turn the <color=#00E1FFFF>clockwork key</color> over there? I'll explain everything in a bit.

talks.objective: Turn the gear and save the toy man

dialogues.speaker: Bleucher
dialogues.text: Ahh... Th—Thank you, thank you...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What happened there? It almost seemed like we turned back time...

dialogues.speaker: Bleufond
dialogues.text: I take it this is your first time witnessing the power of the Goddess of Prophecy, then? If so, I can see why you might think that.

dialogues.speaker: Bleufond
dialogues.text: Basically, this is a gift bestowed upon Constellation Metropole by the Goddess of Prophecy, who rules over the natural course of all things. It helps those who have deviated from their proper path to get back on track.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Proper path? ...Do you mean, everything that happens in the Metropole has been planned out since the very beginning?

dialogues.speaker: Bleufond
dialogues.text: ...Why are you saying that as if it's a bad thing?

dialogues.speaker: Bleucher
dialogues.text: You're not explaining it clearly — here, allow me... Of course, all residents of the Metropole have the freedom to live their own lives. For instance, whether I use olive oil or sesame oil in my morning skincare routine is entirely my choice.

dialogues.speaker: Bleucher
dialogues.text: But whenever something disastrous is about to happen — like, when I almost got turned into a pile of rubble just now — the Goddess's magic will activate in the world around us.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So in other words, it's a kind of... protection magic? To keep people alive?

dialogues.speaker: Bleufond
dialogues.text: You could say that... There are other situations in which it activates, too, but that's basically correct.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Well, in any case, we're glad no one's hurt.

dialogues.speaker: Bleucher
dialogues.text: Are you heading to Constellation Metropole?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yup! Do you know where we can find the Gear Sky Ladder?

dialogues.speaker: Bleucher
dialogues.text: Oh, it's just that platform up ahead — the one with the key sticking out.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? That thing? Umm... Are you sure?

dialogues.speaker: Bleufond
dialogues.text: Yep, that's the one! Pretty much everything in the Metropole runs on tracks and gears. The Goddess of Prophecy watches over it all.

dialogues.speaker: Bleufond
dialogues.text: Which is to say, all the tracks are fixed. If a machine is set up to move forwards, it will never move in reverse.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This reminds Paimon a lot of Fontaine's clockwork toys.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: You mean, like those music boxes with dancing figures? I think I've seen one or two from the merchants in Sumeru.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, exactly like that. Anyway, sounds like it's not gonna suddenly fall out of the sky, so Paimon's okay now. Should we get going?

talks.objective: Turn the gear and save the toy man
Go to the Gear Sky Ladder
Go to Constellation Metropole

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, what a bustling city! This place is fit for a king!

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Our next step is to get to the top of the Metropole, and ask the Goddess of Prophecy for guidance. If there is a king in that castle, I sure hope he won't get mad at us for trespassing...

dialogues.speaker: Toy Guard
dialogues.text: Make way for the King!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, darn, we jinxed it... Oh no, did he overhear us talking about us sneaking into his castle? Paimon hopes he's not mad...

dialogues.speaker: Toy Guard
dialogues.text: Silence!

dialogues.speaker: Toy Guard
dialogues.text: The one who shall soon stand before you is the ruler of Constellation Metropole, the one who descended after a meteor shower, and the protector of order and all the stars in the sky...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's a long list of titles...
I bid ye welcome, guests from afar!
Long have I heard of your grand deeds, O Fairy, who restored the lifeblood of the Forest, O Hero, who... Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Navia!?

dialogues.speaker: Toy Guard
dialogues.text: Hold your foul tongue! How dare you utter Her Majesty's name?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Hahaha, nice one, partner! Spectacular improvisation skills — I'd expect no less from you!

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: #Alright, alright, you can relax now. Allow me to make some introductions. This is {NICKNAME}, and {M#his}{F#her} trusty companion, Paimon.

response.speaker: Toy Guard
response.text: You are personal friends with Her Majesty the King? Please, forgive our grievous mistake! We had no idea.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Ahem...! Alright, the welcome ceremony is over. Everyone, back to your stations. I will personally treat our guests to some royal hospitality.

response.speaker: Toy Guard
response.text: Yes, Your Majesty!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Your Majesty, we are most grateful for your—

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Come on, I've already sent them off. So anyway, how did you guys get here?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We were gonna ask you the same thing... Also, how are you already king of this nation? And where did you get a crown? ...Oh, wait, don't say it — you just woke up like this, right?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Sounds like you've answered your own question. But before I woke up, I heard a voice say to me: "You are the king of Constellation Metropole. Now go forth and save your city."

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: A similar thing happened to me.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Oh yeah, sorry — you must be the Fairy of the Forest of Blessings, right?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Mhm! This is Nilou, a friend we made during our time in Sumeru.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Nice to meet you, Miss Nilou! I'm Navia, the President of Spina di Rosula. If you ever get the chance to go to Fontaine, make sure you come and visit me! I'm based in Poisson.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Seems like you're taking this all in stride... Aren't you nervous about getting stuck here and never being able to get back home?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Why would I be worried about that? We've faced much bigger problems than this before, and we always pull through. This should be a piece of cake!

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Besides, life's always full of surprises. You gotta learn to just enjoy it!

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: That sounds like a great outlook on life. You have a very optimistic spirit.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Thanks! I'll take that. Honestly though, it also puts me at ease to find out that you guys are the "Fairy" and "Heroes" that I've been hearing about in this prophecy. Heh, we're kinda veterans at dealing with prophecies by now, aren't we?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: About that, has anything bad happened in the Metropole? We heard about an evil dragon, did it make a mess here too?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: It sure did. Apparently, for whatever reason, he went for the stars above the city recently. Literally just flew up and starting snatching them out of the sky!

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Luckily, the guards responded quickly, and stopped the dragon from taking them back to his lair. Unfortunately, though, he dropped them before he flew off. Now they're scattered all around the Metropole.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: I've been out trying to retrieve them, but I only managed to get one of them before you showed up... Oh, I didn't ask yet — what brings you to the Metropole, anyway?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, Paimon can explain...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Huh, I see... So you want to consult the oracle of the Goddess of Prophecy.

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: Do you know how we can do that, Miss Navia?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Well, the Goddess's statue is indeed at the top of the castle. I can take you up there.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: However, I've heard from the citizens here that the Goddess hasn't given out any new revelations in a very long time.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Really? But Grandpa Almond told us that he received his prophecy from the Goddess...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Oh, that's probably because the prophecy about the "Hero of Simulanka" has been around for a very long time.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: But recently, people realized that the Goddess didn't reveal anything about what's supposed to happen after peace has been restored.

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: Huh, okay...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Still, can't hurt to try your luck. And maybe you can help me get rid of the invaders while we're at it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Invaders? So the dragon's not your only problem?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Right. The Forest isn't the only place where strange things have been happening to the residents. Have you come across the "gift from the Goddess of Prophecy" yet?

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: You mean, the protection magic that stops them from coming to harm? We saw it in action.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Yep, that's the one. Over the past little while, this magic has been triggering far more frequently. We don't know if it's simply because the Metropole has grown a lot more dangerous, or if there's a deeper reason behind it.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Some residents find themselves getting stuck in place and unable to move, others start repeating the same thing over and over again, like they're trapped in some kind of loop.

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: If we were to use clockwork toys as an analogy, could it be that the tracks have eroded, or the gears have slid out of place?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: That's exactly right, Nilou. That's basically what's happening.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Anyway, some of the monsters outside the city saw this as an opportunity to launch an invasion.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? But we didn't see a single monster on our way here.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: That's because I already took care of most of them over the past couple of days. Of the remaining few, we trapped some of them inside the castle and chased the rest back out of the city.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay, so to summarize... Not only has the magic here gotten all messed up, but the dragon's also knocked some of the stars out of the sky, plus there's a bunch of monsters in the city...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Sounds like there's a lot more to fix here than in the Forest of Blessings.

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: Well, defeating the dragon and the monsters should be straightforward enough... But how do we fix the magic?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Supposedly, the Goddess has had it all planned out for ages. One of her oldest prophecies says this:

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: "...Go, and push the gear that connects up to the starry sky. When that time comes, I shall dance, and return the tracks beneath my people's feet back to the stars in the sky."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? But weren't the "tracks" the gift that she gave to her people in the first place? Does that mean she plans to take the gift back?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: That's what the prophecy seems to be saying, yes. So as a result, some people are against turning the gear, despite what the prophecy says, since they fear a future where they no longer enjoy the Goddess's protection.

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: But letting this drag on isn't the answer either, is it...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: No. And I think they know that, but they're just too afraid to take that final, terrifying step... They're still hoping there might be an alternative solution.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Now, we could ignore their objections and go turn the gear ourselves, but...

choices.text: You want to be considerate of their feelings...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Exactly! You know me well, and that's why you're my partner!

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: I want to get as many people on my side as possible. At the end of the day, this is their city, and they should have the right to decide its future.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ooh! Spoken like a true, wise king, Navia!

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: I am the Boss of Spina di Rosula, after all. This may be my first time as a king, but there are a few similarities between the two roles.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, Miss Nilou... Would you be willing to lend me your support?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: With your help, I'm confident we'll be able to find the most frictionless way to resolve the problems plaguing this city.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Thanks, partner!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Seriously, like we'd ever say no! We're your friends. No need to ask us so formally in the future.

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: I'm happy to help, too. This is a beautiful city, and just like the Forest of Blessings, I would love to see it return to normal as soon as possible.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Ah, great! As the King of Constellation Metropole, I extend to you my gratitude.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Alright, everyone follow me — I'll show you the way to the Goddess Statue <color=#00E1FFFF>at the top of the Metropole</color>. And stay close! You don't wanna get lost in my castle, it's huge!

choices.text: It would be my honor, Your Majesty.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Hahaha! Not gonna lie, "Your Majesty" is definitely growing on me...

choices.text: You want to let them make that choice for themselves.

talks.objective: Follow Navia to the designated location

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? What's this?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Wait, this looks like the <color=#00E1FFFF>star</color> I found earlier. I told the guards to place it near the Goddess Statue... Maybe they ran into some trouble up there.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Guess we'd better hurry.

talks.objective: Go to the city's highest point

dialogues.speaker: Montagne
dialogues.text: Drat... I can't move...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: What happened?

dialogues.speaker: Montagne
dialogues.text: Your Majesty! This... conservative radical, he attacked us! He threw the star from the Astral Garden, and even stole the Magic Thread linking the Oracle Pillars...

dialogues.speaker: Montagne
dialogues.text: But just as we were about to arrest him, the Goddess's magic activated, and now we can't move...

dialogues.speaker: Olivier
dialogues.text: No! Nobody touch the celestial gear!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What's an "Oracle Pillar"?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: You need to use it to pray to the Goddess... I'll explain later — first, let's help these guys!

talks.objective: Turn the gear and capture the suspicious person
Talk to the Guard Captain

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey! He's getting away!

dialogues.speaker: Montagne
dialogues.text: Halt!

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: It's okay! Let him go.

dialogues.speaker: Montagne
dialogues.text: But... Your Majesty!

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Even if we catch up to him now, we won't be able to change his mind, much less quell the fear that many others like him are feeling. All it would do is turn him further against us.

dialogues.speaker: Montagne
dialogues.text: ...Understood, Your Majesty.

dialogues.speaker: Montagne
dialogues.text: Also, this is the Magic Thread he was holding, from the Oracle Pillars. Your Majesty, what should we...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: #Mhm, you can give it to {NICKNAME} over there. They seem to have some questions that they'd like to ask the Goddess.

dialogues.speaker: Montagne
dialogues.text: Yes, Your Majesty.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um... So what do we do with this, exactly?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: See those Oracle Pillars over there? Just use the Magic Thread to <color=#00E1FFFF>connect them together in a specific pattern</color>, and the Goddess of Prophecy will answer your prayers.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, sounds easy enough. Let's give it a try!

talks.objective: Connect the Oracle Pillars to thread them into a specific shape
Seeks answers from the Goddess of Prophecy

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Then first, we have to restore the sky back to its original state by putting the stars back in their positions. But it looks like we haven't recovered all the lost stars yet.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Well, at least we know what we're looking for now. We just need to keep going. That said... the Metropole is huge, where do we even start?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Oh, that's the easy part. I already compiled a list of the lost stars' locations based on eyewitness reports from across the city. Here you go, they should all be marked.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Would you mind going around and fetching them for me? I have a few other things to take care of.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You got it! We'll be back in no time.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Awesome. In that case, meet me back here once you've found <color=#00E1FFFF>them all</color>.

talks.objective: Seek the scattered stars

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: ...It worked!

dialogues.speaker: Statue of the Goddess of Prophecy
Statue of the Goddess of Prophecy
dialogues.text: ...To which course of fate do you seek answers, my child of Simulanka?

choices.text: Ask how to leave this world

response.speaker: Statue of the Goddess of Prophecy
Nilou
response.text: So, Miss Navia was right... The Goddess of Prophecy didn't tell us anything about the future.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Fair enough... Guess we'll just have to play it by ear.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: If we want to push the celestial gear...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Then first, we have to restore the sky back to its original state by putting the stars back in their positions. Let me do a quick count...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Alright! Adding in the ones we picked up on the way here, I think that's all of them! Let's go hang these stars back up in the sky!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: In the sky...? How do we get up there?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Hehe, I got us covered! We will, of course, be taking... the Aerial Express!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Is that a flying train!?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Hey, you already took a train that runs on water. Is a flying train really that much weirder?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Well, at least the Maritime Express still runs on a track!

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Oh, c'mon, don't worry about it! This train has been blessed by the Goddess of Prophecy. Its whole purpose is to protect the Metropole's skies.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: It took me a lot of effort to find it, you know... I don't think anyone's used it in, like... a hundred years?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: A hundred years!? Are you sure it's safe? Let's not forget that the Goddess of Prophecy's magic has been going haywire recently...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Well... It's not like we have any other options. Unless you wanna do the honors, Paimon? Fancy flying up there on your own?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Nooo thank you! It's way too high up... Wait, Nilou, you've got a feel for how magic works here. Can you do your thing and sense if this train is the real deal?

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: I can try... Hmm... Yes, I can sense traces of magic, but it's different from the kind I felt in the Forest. So... I don't know.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay, fine... Guess there's only one way to find out.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: That's the spirit! I'll come with you. Miss Nilou, will you be joining us?

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: I think I'll stay behind. That way, if something does go wrong, you'll have someone on the ground to get you some help.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That makes sense! If the train does break down, you can make us a giant origami crane to come bail us out! ...Or if a crane's too difficult, a Finch could work!

choices.text: Ask how to defeat the dragon

response.speaker: Statue of the Goddess of Prophecy
response.text: The Hero from another world, supported by their companions, shall restore peace to this world...

response.speaker: Statue of the Goddess of Prophecy

choices.text: Ask how to resolve the Metropole's crisis

response.speaker: Statue of the Goddess of Prophecy
response.text: ...Go, and push the gear that connects up to the starry sky. When that time comes, I shall dance, and return the tracks beneath my people's feet back to the stars in the sky.

talks.objective: Seek the scattered stars

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: How are you doing? Found them all?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Sure, no worries. I'll be right here, so just come find me once you've retrieved them. I'm counting on you!

talks.objective: Seek the scattered stars

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Best of luck! Hmm... a finch, huh? I think I know how to fold one of those...

talks.objective: Return to the highest point of the city and speak with Navia

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Wow, you guys are efficient! Now, let's go hang 'em up in the sky!

talks.objective: Seeks answers from the Goddess of Prophecy
Ride the Aerial Express
Ride the Aerial Express
Restore the stars to their positions
Return to the city's highest point

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Great job! It looked like it all went smoothly.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Yeah! And it was an absolute blast, too. You gotta ride with us next time, Miss Nilou!

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Huh? Ah, I'm okay, thanks...

dialogues.speaker: Montagne
dialogues.text: Halt! What do you think you're doing!?

dialogues.speaker: Olivier
dialogues.text: Get out of my way!

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: What's going on?

dialogues.speaker: Montagne
dialogues.text: Your Majesty, they're...

dialogues.speaker: Olivier
dialogues.text: Let us through!

dialogues.speaker: Montagne
dialogues.text: Stay back!

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: It's okay. Let them through.

dialogues.speaker: Olivier
dialogues.text: Y—Your Majesty... Could we please ask you.... not to turn the gear that connects up to the sky?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: And why is that?

dialogues.speaker: Olivier
dialogues.text: ...As you have seen, the Goddess's gift is very important to us. It keeps us from harm, and protects our very lives.

dialogues.speaker: Bizerte
dialogues.text: Some of us... we just aren't ready to lose that protection.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: ...I see. I understand.

dialogues.speaker: Bizerte
dialogues.text: Huh? Y—Your Majesty... Do you mean...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: I won't turn that gear... Not until you're ready.

dialogues.speaker: Olivier
dialogues.text: ...What?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: I've said before that the Metropole belongs to the people, and they should have the right to decide its future.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: But let me ask you this: How do you plan to solve the issues we are currently facing?

dialogues.speaker: Olivier
dialogues.text: Well, we'll start by rescuing the people that have gotten stuck! And then... we'll find a way to figure out the true cause of this crisis!

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: And have you made any headway on that? The true cause, I mean?

dialogues.speaker: Bizerte
dialogues.text: ...Unfortunately not.

dialogues.speaker: Olivier
dialogues.text: Hey! You little...!

dialogues.speaker: Bizerte
dialogues.text: I'm sorry, my friend, but it's the truth...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: You have friends and family that have been affected, don't you? That have gotten stuck?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: ...I understand your concerns. But if we let this drag on for much longer, the situation may well get worse. More and more people will be frozen by the Goddess's magic.

dialogues.speaker: Olivier
dialogues.text: Yes, but... if we turn that gear now, all the tracks in this city will disappear!

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: I know this is a hard decision to make. But have you ever thought about why the Goddess might have made things this way in the first place?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Why do you think she might decide to take back her gift, and stop revealing further prophecies about the future?

dialogues.speaker: Olivier
dialogues.text: Are you saying... She has abandoned us?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: No. Quite the opposite, in fact.

dialogues.speaker: Olivier
dialogues.text: ...What do you mean?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: The Goddess dearly loves this world and all the people of Simulanka. And because she loves you so much... she wants you to be able to choose your own path.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Every parent hopes their child will have a happy and carefree life. But if they're overprotective, then all they'll manage to do is keep their child trapped.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: If a mother bird lets her baby ride on her wings for too long, her child will never learn how to fly. Perhaps the Goddess of Prophecy has always known that one day... she'll have to let go.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Children can only become independent if they're allowed to form their own opinions, make their own decisions, and deal with the consequences on their own. Only then will they be able to continue their journey alone, even after their parents are gone.

dialogues.speaker: Bizerte
dialogues.text: ...But, we've relied on the Goddess's protection for so long... We don't know what it's like to go it alone. We don't know if we have what it takes.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Are you kidding me? I think you've proven yourselves more than capable of that.

dialogues.speaker: Bizerte
dialogues.text: What do you mean...?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: You made a call in a time of crisis, and you've come all this way to talk to me. Even the guards couldn't stop you. That must have taken a lot of courage!

dialogues.speaker: Bizerte
dialogues.text: But... We only did it because we were scared...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Why you set out on the journey doesn't matter. What matters is that you've proven you can choose your own path.

dialogues.speaker: Bizerte
dialogues.text: ...My friend, I fear our King is right. It is time for us to face our fears.

dialogues.speaker: Olivier
dialogues.text: What!? But... But we...

dialogues.speaker: Bizerte
dialogues.text: We can't go on living like this, living in fear! Look at what it's driven you to do... You threw away a star personally created by the Goddess of Prophecy herself!

dialogues.speaker: Bizerte
dialogues.text: You once revered her more than any of us. And I think the King is right — she hasn't abandoned us. So... why don't we put our trust in her one more time?

dialogues.speaker: Olivier
dialogues.text: ...I don't care anymore! Do what you want!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah... He left...

dialogues.speaker: Bizerte
dialogues.text: I'm sorry about my friend... That's just how he is. Always had a terrible temper. Please accept my apology for his impudent behavior.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Is it just me, or... has he accepted the Goddess's prophecy?

dialogues.speaker: Bizerte
dialogues.text: I think so. Not that you'll ever hear him admit it out loud.

dialogues.speaker: Bizerte
dialogues.text: Your Majesty... Please, turn the gear that connects up to the sky.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: So you've made up your mind? About giving up the Goddess's gift?

dialogues.speaker: Bizerte
dialogues.text: Yes, I've made up my mind. But maybe losing the gift isn't what this is about anymore. Because we've gained something, too... you have given us courage.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Hehe, well said. I am proud of your decision!

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Now, gather around, everyone, and join me as we make the night sky of this wonderful city turn once more!

talks.objective: Talk to the group

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: So the stars hanging in the sky... they're music notes!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This entire Metropole is a huge music box... That's incredible!

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: How do you feel?

dialogues.speaker: Bizerte
dialogues.text: ...A little scared and uncertain, but for some reason, I feel a lot more at ease. It's as if... some kind of huge weight has been lifted from my shoulders.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Figured out any next steps?

dialogues.speaker: Bizerte
dialogues.text: To be honest, not really... But maybe I can start by having a heart to heart with that stubborn friend of mine.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: I have an idea! If you don't know what to do, why don't you start by helping the people around you?

dialogues.speaker: Bizerte
dialogues.text: ...You mean, the people who got stuck because of the Goddess's magic?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: I mean anyone and everyone who needs your help! By helping others, you'll eventually find your own path. Trust me, I have experience in this!

dialogues.speaker: Bizerte
dialogues.text: ...What kind of experience, Your Majesty?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Hmm... Ah yes, we'll need a formal organization with a catchy name before we go out and start helping people... Why don't we call it the Spina di Rosula?

dialogues.speaker: Bizerte
dialogues.text: Spina... di Rosula?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Ooh, or even: the Spina di Rosula di Simulanka! Yeah, that's catchy!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, big expansion for the Spina... moving into other worlds now!

dialogues.speaker: Bizerte
dialogues.text: Spina di Rosula... Haha, I like it! It's a great name. Let's do as Your Majesty suggests!

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Well then, how about I appoint you as the head of the Spina in Simulanka? While I'm off fighting the dragon with the other heroes, it'll be your responsibility to work with the guards and take good care of the people in the Metropole.

dialogues.speaker: Montagne
dialogues.text: What? You're planning on fighting the dragon!? But... No, Your Majesty, you must reconsider!

dialogues.speaker: Bizerte
dialogues.text: He's right! Your Majesty, you can't!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: How are you two on the same side all of a sudden...

dialogues.speaker: Bizerte
dialogues.text: Perhaps Your Majesty is unaware of this... The great dragon suddenly broke out from the toytanium mines one day, and tore <color=#00E1FFFF>the end of the world</color> to pieces.

dialogues.speaker: Bizerte
dialogues.text: After that, it spat out a strange fog that surrounded a whole island. No one knows what lies beyond the fog, and no one knows what has become of that poor island...

dialogues.speaker: Montagne
dialogues.text: Before Your Majesty arrived, we dispatched many soldiers to fight the dragon, but... none came back alive.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yikes, sounds worse than we thought...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Isn't that all the more reason for us to go? There could still be guards trapped there, waiting for someone to rescue them!

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: King Navia is right. We cannot simply stand by and watch as the people of this world suffer.

dialogues.speaker: Montagne
dialogues.text: Very well. Though I have not served by your side for very long, Your Majesty, two days is enough for me to have learned that once your mind is set, any attempts to change it are futile.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Haha! You're a pretty good judge of character.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um... He probably didn't mean that as a compliment...

dialogues.speaker: Montagne
dialogues.text: Since you're serious about this, I won't try and stop you... There's only one way to reach the end of the world, and that's by taking the Maritime Express.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Oh, right! So there's a line going there too?

dialogues.speaker: Montagne
dialogues.text: Yes. It was originally built to serve the workers commuting to the toytanium mines, but it has been abandoned since the dragon attack.

dialogues.speaker: Montagne
dialogues.text: I'll tell the conductor to wait for you at the platform <color=#00E1FFFF>by the side gate of the Metropole</color>, first thing tomorrow morning. You are embarking on an extremely dangerous adventure... Please be careful, Your Majesty and friends.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Thank you for your concern. While I'm gone, I leave the Metropole in your capable hands.

dialogues.speaker: Both
dialogues.text: Yes, Your Majesty!

dialogues.speaker: Guard Captain & Sensible Conservative Citizen
dialogues.text: Yes, Your Majesty.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Hehe, just call me "Boss" from now on. That's what everyone in the Spina calls me, and it's what I'm used to.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So the plan for tomorrow is... journey across the ocean, make it to the end of the world, and defeat a dragon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Phew... That's an adventure and a half. Do all storybook heroes have to work this hard?

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: At least we'll get to see some amazing scenery along the way, right? Besides, we'll have each other. It'll be a shared experience that we'll never forget.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Plus, we're pretty well-equipped for a classic heroes-versus-dragon story. We got Miss Nilou as our magic caster, and I... I guess I'm the melee warrior who leads the charge?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon can definitely see that...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Anyway, those are tomorrow's problems! Right now, all Paimon wants is to eat a proper meal. Because worst case scenario, if Paimon ends up getting eaten by a dragon, she wants to do it on a full stomach. And something about "the end of the world" doesn't sound like a great place for food options.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Hmm... Well, the origami animals in the Forest only drink Magic Tonic... What do the toy people here in Constellation Metropole eat?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Vegetable oil and sawdust, I think.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Noooooo!!

talks.objective: Additional

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Morning! Guess everything that happened yesterday wasn't just a dream, then...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, it's time for our next fairytale adventure! We should head to the station Grandpa Almond told us about...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Onwards and upwards... Let's head to that Gear Sky Ladder thing that Wheel mentioned.
Help me! Somebody, please!

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Over there! Somebody needs our help!
